title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 241
text:
111. There are different views as to whether a person should be referred to as a “disabled
person” or a “person with a disability”. The former formulation, although unpopular at one
stage, has been generally adopted by disability groups as it puts the focus on the barriers
imposed by society. In other English-speaking countries, people prefer to use “people with
disabilities”. Disabled people do not always use the same language, and it is advisable to
ask the person what term they prefer.

112. Some Acts of Parliament, particularly older ones, use terminology that would now be
considered out of date and, in some cases, inappropriate. Judicial office holders will continue
to work with those statutory definitions and tests until such time as the legislation is
updated. Whilst legal findings must continue to be phrased within the technical definitions,
